newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu party ready to share power with Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu party ready to share power with Zaire rebels.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's party said on Tuesday it was ready to "share power" with Laurent Kabila's rebels ahead of elections.
"We shall meet and after dialogue we will share power," Banza Mukalayi, vice-chairman of Mobutu's MPR party, told Reuters in Kinshasa.

His comments went much further than previous signs that the ailing Mobutu and his Popular Revolutionary Movement (MPR) were ready to seek a deal with Kabila's rebels who now control nearly a quarter of Zaire.
"First we will talk to find the mechanism for a ceasefire and then we will share power before elections," Banza said.
Under Mobutu's laborious and grudging moves to democracy after 32 years in power, Zaire is supposed to hold its first real multiparty elections by July.
The deadline was ambitious before Kabila's rebellion began last October but looks fanciful now that the rebels control the east of Zaire and are surging forward on several fronts.
But both sides are under mounting pressure to stop the civil war, agree a ceasefire and enter negotiations.
The pressure will intensify at an African summit in Togo on Wednesday attended by the U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
